short: The demon king slain by Vishnu’s lion-man form.
note: Hiranyakashipu is the demon king overcome by Narasimha, Vishnu’s incarnation with a human body and a lion’s head.

sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Narasimha and Hiranyakashipu

short: Hindu deity and an incarnation of Vishnu.
note: A widely worshipped Hindu deity, traditionally an incarnation of Vishnu. His youthful feats include lifting Mount Govardhana to shelter cowherds and cattle from Indra’s storm.

sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: South and Southeast Asian art

short: Vedic god associated with storms and rain.
note: A major Vedic deity associated with the heavens, rain, and the thunderbolt. In the Govardhana episode, Krishna shelters the cowherds from a storm sent by Indra.

sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: South and Southeast Asian art

short: The ruler of Mathura opposed by Krishna.
note: The tyrant of Mathura in Krishna’s childhood legends, who tries to destroy the infant destined to overthrow him.

sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Krishna enters Mathura

short: The Nome King of L. Frank Baum’s Oz books.
note: The underground ruler called the Nome King in L. Frank Baum’s Oz books, notably Ozma of Oz (1907). His realm is rich in metals and jewels.

sources.label: L. Frank Baum: Ozma of Oz

short: Possibly the Scarecrow of The Wizard of Oz.
note: Possibly the Scarecrow, the straw-filled companion who seeks brains in L. Frank Baum’s The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900).

sources.label: L. Frank Baum: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz

short: Possibly the Tin Woodman of The Wizard of Oz.
note: Possibly the Tin Woodman, Dorothy’s metal-bodied companion who seeks a heart in L. Frank Baum’s The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900).

sources.label: L. Frank Baum: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz

short: The Kansas girl of The Wizard of Oz.
note: Dorothy is the Kansas girl carried by a cyclone to Oz in L. Frank Baum’s The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), accompanied by her dog Toto.

sources.label: L. Frank Baum: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz

short: Relating to B. F. Skinner’s behavioral psychology.
note: Relating to psychologist B. F. Skinner and his analysis of operant conditioning: behavior becomes more or less likely according to its consequences.

sources.label: B. F. Skinner Foundation: operant behavior

short: A god or divine being in Indian religions.
note: A Sanskrit term for a god or celestial being, used in Hinduism and Buddhism.

sources.label: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: deva

short: Possibly Pṛthivī, the personified earth.
note: Possibly Pṛthivī, Sanskrit for the earth or wide world and the name of its female divine personification.

sources.label: Monier-Williams Sanskrit-English Dictionary: pṛthivī

short: The Hindu preserver of cosmic order.
note: A major Hindu deity associated with preserving cosmic order, appearing in incarnations that include Krishna and the lion-man Narasimha.

sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: South and Southeast Asian art

short: Krishna’s mother in Hindu tradition.
note: The mother of Krishna, who is taken from prison as a newborn and raised by Yashoda to protect him from King Kamsa.

sources.label: National Museum, New Delhi: birth of Krishna

short: The Japanese tradition of reverence for kami.
note: Shinto, Japan’s religious tradition centered on reverence for kami, including divine powers of nature and ancestral spirits, with worship at shrines called jinja.

sources.label: Jinja Honcho: What is Shinto?

short: A curved Japanese sword.
note: A Japanese sword with a curved, single-edged blade, traditionally worn edge upward through the sash.

sources.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: katana

short: The fourteenth-century Swedish mystic.
note: Bridget or Birgitta of Sweden (1303–1373), a Christian mystic whose visions were collected as Revelations and who founded the religious order known as the Bridgettines.

sources.label: Vatican: Saint Bridget of Sweden

short: The author of the Narnia books.
note: The British writer and Christian apologist whose Chronicles of Narnia feature Aslan, a great lion associated with creation, sacrifice, and resurrection.

sources.label: C. S. Lewis official site: biography

short: A catch that prevents backward motion.
note: A pivoting catch that engages the teeth or notches of a wheel, allowing motion in one direction and blocking the reverse.

sources.label: Merriam-Webster: pawl

short: A story by Anatole France about Pontius Pilate.
note: Anatole France’s short story in which the retired Roman governor Pontius Pilate recalls his service in Judea.

sources.label: Anatole France: The Procurator of Judea

short: Glowing outlines in electrical-discharge photographs.
note: Kirlian photography records corona discharges around objects subjected to high voltage. A 1976 study found that moisture accounted for much of the variation in images of living subjects.

sources.label: Pehek, Kyler, and Faust: Image modulation in corona discharge photography (reprinted abstract)
